brief.greeting: Good morning. OpenAI just slashed token prices again, and the math feels like a cheat code.

stories.headline: GPT-6.1 Sol costs a fifth of Astra
stories.body: **Token price shock:** GPT-6.1 Sol offers near‑Astra coding ability while charging only one‑fifth the input and output token price of Astra. The lower cost could make high‑end LLM use affordable for more teams.
stories.why: Cheaper tokens let you run more inference cycles without blowing your cloud bill.

stories.headline: UserProxyBench reveals 15‑point reward swing
stories.body: **User fidelity matters:** Swapping user simulators across 375 enterprise tasks changes mean task reward by 15.2 points, and 24.4% of successful runs break user specs. The new User Fidelity Score quantifies that drift.
stories.why: Understanding proxy quality helps you trust agent evaluations before deployment.

stories.headline: SPLASH enables live attention layout swaps
stories.body: **No downtime serving:** SPLASH lets a running LLM switch its parallel attention layout on the fly, avoiding worker drains and restarts. It keeps requests flowing while the backend reconfigures.
stories.why: Zero‑downtime layout changes mean higher throughput for your inference fleet.

quick_hits.text: **Meta‑reasoning:** New controller makes stepwise choices explicit, trimming run histories.
**LongHarness:** Benchmark stresses long‑context harnesses with retrieval and adaptive tasks.
**CHERI compartments:** Model scales to over 10K in‑process compartments on UNIX.
**Rust compiler:** RLX unifies tensor compilation and distributed runtime in Rust.

highlights.title: UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training
highlights.summary: UserProxyBench adds a User Fidelity Score and shows that swapping the user proxy across 375 enterprise tasks shifts mean task reward by 15.2 points, with 24.4% of successful episodes violating user specifications.
highlights.detail: The benchmark sits on top of the tau-bench family and evaluates the simulated user independently of agent success. The most common error is premature disclosure, where the user reveals information before being asked. This highlights the need for better user modeling in agent evaluations.

highlights.title: Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning
highlights.summary: The paper proposes agentic meta-reasoning, an inference-time controller that makes stepwise execution choices explicit and keeps only a compact run summary instead of replaying full history.
highlights.detail: The system separates workers that perform task-level computation from a controller that consolidates progress, explores options, assesses budget impact, and dispatches work with context from persistent memory. Baselines include production coding agents and a Direct Control Agent using the same resources.

highlights.title: LongHarness Bench: Stress-Testing Language Model Harnesses for Long-Context Reasoning
highlights.summary: LongHarness Bench introduces a benchmark to assess both effectiveness and efficiency of long-context language model harnesses using diverse retrieval and adaptive reasoning tasks.
highlights.detail: Current long-context evaluations show saturated accuracy, making it hard to differentiate harnesses. The new benchmark requires lexical and semantic search, and only a small subset of the large context is useful at each step, creating varied accuracy‑cost trade‑offs.

items.title: DevDay 2026 Recap
items.summary: OpenAI DevDay 2026 announced more than 20 new features, including GPT-6 Astra, updates to ChatGPT and Codex, new APIs, security enhancements, and builder tools.
items.detail: The announcements span improvements in model capabilities, developer access, and safety measures, aiming to broaden the ecosystem for both consumer and enterprise applications. Specific product roadmaps were outlined for upcoming releases.

items.title: Introducing GPT-6.1 Sol
items.summary: GPT-6.1 Sol delivers near‑Astra coding and professional work intelligence at one‑fifth the standard API input and output token prices of Astra.
items.detail: Positioned as a cost‑effective alternative, Sol targets developers needing high‑quality code generation and computer‑use assistance while reducing operational expenses. It retains most of Astra’s performance characteristics for coding tasks.

items.title: Getting the Source Right, Not Just the Fact: Source-Aware Verification for MCP Agents
items.summary: The article presents source‑aware verification techniques for MCP agents to ensure generated facts are backed by correct sources.
items.detail: It outlines methods for integrating source checking into agent pipelines, improving reliability of multi‑chain processing (MCP) agents. The approach aims to reduce hallucinations by tying each claim to verifiable evidence.

items.title: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular Sets a New Accuracy-Efficiency Frontier for Tabular Prediction
items.summary: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular is a new model for tabular prediction that claims higher accuracy while using less compute than prior approaches.
items.detail: The model targets common tabular benchmarks and is positioned as a frontier in the accuracy‑efficiency trade‑off, aiming to reduce inference cost for production workloads.

items.title: Model: SupersonicLabs/Julia-1
items.summary: SupersonicLabs/Julia-1 is a text‑classification model on Hugging Face with 1,725 downloads and 302 likes.
items.detail: The model is listed under the HF trending section and is intended for general text classification tasks, showing modest community interest.

items.title: Model: apple/LensVLM-9B
items.summary: apple/LensVLM-9B is an image‑text‑to‑text model on Hugging Face with 1,956 downloads and 268 likes.
items.detail: LensVLM-9B combines visual and language capabilities, targeting multimodal generation scenarios, and has attracted a moderate number of users on the platform.

items.title: [$] The kernel from a PostgreSQL point of view
items.summary: Andres Freund discussed PostgreSQL performance and kernel interactions at the 2026 Kernel Recipes conference.
items.detail: Freund highlighted how Linux kernel features affect database workloads and suggested improvements to better support PostgreSQL, referencing recent developments in both projects.

items.title: Security updates for Tuesday
items.summary: Security updates were released Tuesday for multiple Linux distributions, covering dozens of packages.
items.detail: Distributions including AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Slackware, SUSE, and Ubuntu published patches for components such as kernels, libraries, and server software to address recent vulnerabilities.

items.title: Firefox 157.0 released
items.summary: Firefox version 157.0 was released, adding a visual refresh and hardware AV1 decoding for WebRTC.
items.detail: The update also includes numerous bug fixes and performance improvements, marking the most significant UI overhaul in years while enhancing media handling capabilities.

items.title: [$] Native support for Rust on the GPU
items.summary: Rust GPU maintainer Christian Legnitto showcased a prototype aiming to make GPUs a native compiler target for standard Rust code, eliminating the need for special libraries.
items.detail: The prototype builds on rust-gpu and Rust CUDA but extends them to support ordinary Rust without additional ecosystem layers. Legnitto presented this vision at RustConf 2026, indicating future work toward full implementation and release. The approach could simplify GPU programming in Rust by leveraging existing compiler infrastructure.

items.title: RLX: A Unified Multi-Backend Tensor Compiler and Distributed Runtime in Rust
items.summary: Production machine learning (ML) stacks often split graph compilation and kernel execution across different layers and languages, making backend behavior, deployment guarantees, and performance fallbacks hard to reason a…
items.detail: Production machine learning (ML) stacks often split graph compilation and kernel execution across different layers and languages, making backend behavior, deployment guarantees, and performance fallbacks hard to reason about end-to-end. RLX addresses this gap with a single Rust codebase that combines compiler and runtime roles around one primitive-level, three-level intermediate representation (IR), plus a transparent dispatch contract that resolves each operator to native, common-IR, or rewritten lowering and fails compilation when legalization is not possible. items.title: SPLASH: Switching Parallel Layouts of Attention with Seamless Handoff for LLM Serving
items.summary: SPLASH is a serving system that can switch the parallel layout of attention for large language models while requests are running, avoiding the need to drain and restart workers.
items.detail: The system leverages the decoupling of KV cache location from attention weight sharding in modern attention implementations, allowing seamless handoff between tensor, data, and context parallelism as workload characteristics change.

items.title: Modelling Shared-Space Coordination in mCRL2: a Bach-to-mCRL2 Translation Framework
items.summary: The authors introduce a translation framework from Bach to mCRL2 to enable model‑checking of shared‑space coordination programs with richer temporal specifications.
items.detail: Existing tools like Anemone only support reachability checks; the new framework aims to verify liveness and invariants such as "every request is matched by a response" and "no message is silently lost", extending verification beyond state attainability.

items.title: DScale: Scaling Block-Diffusion Speculative Decoding with Adaptive Verification
items.summary: DScale improves block‑diffusion speculative decoding by adding a lightweight 112K‑parameter predictor and adaptive verification that halves verification padding on A100‑40GB GPUs.
items.detail: The approach keeps the original drafter architecture and full draft length, using path‑aware tiles and dynamic verify‑length allocation to reuse captured graphs and reduce rejected candidates, showing gains on Qwen3‑8B and Qwen3‑4B across four datasets.

items.title: ccfddl/ccf-deadlines
items.summary: The ccfddl/ccf-deadlines repository provides an agentic tracker for CCF‑ranked and worldwide conference deadlines via website, Python CLI, and WeChat applet.
items.detail: It consolidates deadline information in a single source, enabling developers and researchers to stay up‑to‑date on submission windows without manually checking multiple sites.

items.title: SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX
items.summary: SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX is an open‑source platform that standardizes inference research workflows for Python projects.
items.detail: The repository offers modular components for model loading, benchmarking, and deployment, aiming to reduce duplication of effort across academic and industry inference experiments.

items.title: VectifyAI/PageIndex
items.summary: VectifyAI/PageIndex is a document‑indexing tool designed for vectorless, reasoning‑based retrieval‑augmented generation.
items.detail: By avoiding dense vector embeddings, PageIndex focuses on symbolic reasoning to match passages, supporting use cases where interpretability and logical consistency are prioritized over pure similarity search.

items.title: bytedance/deer-flow
items.summary: bytedance/deer-flow is an open-source long‑horizon SuperAgent framework that coordinates sandboxes, memory, tools, subagents and a message gateway to tackle tasks ranging from minutes to hours.
items.detail: The system is designed to research, code, and create autonomously, integrating multiple skill modules. It aims to handle complex, multi‑step workflows without human intervention, extending prior agent‑oriented architectures.

items.title: cs341-illinois/coursebook
items.summary: cs341-illinois/coursebook is an open-source introductory systems programming textbook used for the University of Illinois CS341 course.
items.detail: The repository provides lecture notes, assignments, and examples covering low‑level programming concepts. It is intended as a free alternative to commercial textbooks and is continuously updated by the course staff.

items.title: debpalash/VoiceStudio
items.summary: debpalash/VoiceStudio is an open-source, fully‑local alternative to ElevenLabs offering voice cloning, design, dubbing, dictation, transcription and audiobook generation in 646 languages.
items.detail: All processing runs on the user's hardware, eliminating cloud‑based privacy concerns. The toolkit includes models for both speech synthesis and recognition, enabling end‑to‑end audio workflows without external services.
